Requirement 9.3.3 of ASVS currently states:


| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **9.3.3** | [ADDED] Verify that mutual TLS (mTLS) is used by services communicating internally within a system or "intra-service communications" to ensure all the involved parties at each end of a network connection are who they claim to be. | | | ✓ | 295 |

While this requirement is essential for securing internal communications, I believe it would be valuable to include a note or recommendation for users managing microservice architectures. In such architectures, managing mTLS certificates manually can be complex, time-consuming, and error-prone. For this reason, adopting a service mesh (such as Istio, Linkerd, or Consul) is often a more scalable and manageable approach for handling mTLS in dynamic microservice environments.

Include guidance or a recommendation in 9.3.3 suggesting that, in microservice architectures, using a service mesh could simplify mTLS management by automating certificate issuance, rotation, and revocation. This would also reduce the risk of configuration errors in a manually managed system, improving both security and operational efficiency.
